extracted.intended_audience: inventors, patent attorneys/agents, and applicants preparing and filing U.S. nonprovisional (utility) patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements for preparing and filing a U.S. nonprovisional (utility) patent application with the USPTO, including required documents, formatting, fees, and drawing/specification/claim standards. Primarily for applicants and practitioners filing in the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional utility patent application must be submitted in the English language or be accompanied by a translation in the English language, a statement that the translation is accurate, and payment of the fee set forth in 37 CFR § 1.17(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If filed in a language other than English without translation/statement/fee, the applicant will receive a notice and time to submit the missing item(s). Any oath/declaration in a language other than English requires an English translation and a statement that the translation is accurate unless in an approved PCT form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required parts of a nonprovisional utility application
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional utility patent application must include a specification (including a description and at least one claim), drawings when necessary, an oath or declaration, and the prescribed filing, search, and examination fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification, claims and abstract constitute the 'complete specification.' Other items (sequence listings, large tables, computer listings) included when applicable. Claims must begin on a new page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable filing methods and avoidance of non-electronic filing fee
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional utility patent application may be filed electronically via Patent Center, by U.S. mail, or by hand delivery. Effective November 15, 2011, regular nonprovisional applications filed by mail or hand-delivery incur a $400 non-electronic filing fee ($200 for small/micro entities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only way to avoid the additional $400 non-electronic filing fee is by filing electronically via Patent Center. Follow-on correspondence filed by non-registered eFilers must be mailed or hand-delivered, and special rules apply to replies to 'Notice of Incomplete Application' to avoid the fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Center and electronic filing format (DOCX) requirements and surcharges
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent Center accepts electronic documents formatted in DOCX and allows the complete specification (description, claims, abstract) to be filed in one DOCX file. Beginning January 17, 2024, the description, claims, and abstract must be filed in DOCX format to avoid a non-DOCX surcharge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-DOCX surcharge is $430 (reduced for small/micro entities). Other application documents (drawings, hand-signed declarations) may be scanned as PDF. Fee per 37 CFR § 1.16(u) applies when written description, claims, and/or abstract do not conform to DOCX requirements. Applicants used to filing PDF specifications must switch to DOCX for nonprovisional filings on/after Jan 17, 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document formatting: page size, margins, spacing, font and numbering
rubrics_metrics.description: Each document must have a top margin of at least 2 cm (3/4 inch), a left margin of at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), right and bottom margins of at least 2 cm (3/4 inch). DOCX document size should be 8.5x11 inches or A4. The specification must have lines 1.5 or double-spaced in a single column; text must be a nonscript font (e.g., Arial, Times Roman, Courier), preferably font size 12. Pages must be numbered consecutively starting with page one (centrally located above or below text).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These formatting requirements apply to the specification (description, claims, abstract). It is desirable to indent paragraphs and number paragraphs (e.g., [0001], [0002], etc.). Failure to meet format requirements can trigger surcharges or nonconforming status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order and minimum elements of a complete application
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete nonprovisional utility patent application should contain elements arranged in the following order: Utility Patent Application Transmittal Form or Transmittal Letter; Appropriate Fees; Application Data Sheet (ADS); Specification (description, at least one claim, abstract); Drawings (when necessary); Executed Oath or Declaration; Nucleotide and Amino Acid Sequence Listing (if necessary); Large Tables or Computer Listings (if necessary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions of each element are provided in the guide. Omitting required elements can result in 'Notice of Incomplete Application' and loss of filing date in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility Patent Application Transmittal Form or Transmittal Letter usage
rubrics_metrics.description: A Utility Patent Application Transmittal Form (Form PTO/AIA/15) or a transmittal letter should be filed to identify the items being filed (specification, drawings, declaration, information disclosure statement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form identifies first named inventor, application type, title, contents, and enclosures. Use Form PTO/SB/21 for correspondence after initial filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment timing and late surcharge
rubrics_metrics.description: Filing, search, and examination fees should be submitted at filing; if paid on a date later than the patent application filing date, a late surcharge of $170 ($68 small entity, $34 micro entity) is owed. The late surcharge also applies if the oath/declaration is filed after the application filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filing via Patent Center, pay online at filing to avoid late surcharge. If paying later by check or money order, make payable to 'Director of the United States Patent and Trademark Office.' If filed without fees, applicant will be notified and required to submit fees plus late surcharge within the time set in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application size fee and excess claims fees
rubrics_metrics.description: For electronic filings, an application size fee is due if total number of specification and drawing pages exceeds 133; for paper filings, size fee due if pages exceed 100. Excess claim fees are due if there are more than three independent claims or more than 20 total claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees are subject to change; consult current fee schedule. Paper filings also incur the non-electronic filing fee referenced above.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee discounts based on Small Entity and Micro Entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Small entity status under 37 CFR § 1.27(a) reduces most patent fees by 60 percent; micro entity status under 37 CFR § 1.29(a) or (d) reduces fees by 80 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must determine appropriateness before asserting status and paying reduced fees. Small entity may be indicated by checking a box on the transmittal form; micro entity requires specific certification forms (PTO/SB/15A or PTO/SB/15B) and detailed certifications. Recommendation: use USPTO micro entity certification forms when claiming micro entity status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Data Sheet (ADS) submission and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of an ADS should be routine and is required in certain instances. For applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, any domestic benefit claim(s) and any foreign priority claim(s) must be made in an ADS within four months from filing or 16 months from the filing date of the prior application, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/AIA/14 is the USPTO's ADS form. See 37 CFR § 1.76 and MPEP § 601.05. Corrected ADS must include underlined text for insertions and strike-through or brackets for deletions. Certain changes cannot be made by corrected ADS alone (e.g., named inventors, correspondence address, foreign priority/domestic benefit information) and must comply with specific CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification: written description, enablement, best mode and claim placement
rubrics_metrics.description: The specification must include a written description of the invention and the manner and process of making and using the invention that concludes with the claims. The specification must be in clear, full, concise, and exact terms to enable any person skilled in the art to make and use the invention. The best mode contemplated by the inventor must be set forth. Claims must begin on a new page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For inventions involving computer programming, program listings may be submitted per 37 CFR § 1.96(b) and (c). Except for reissue or reexamination, pages of the specification (including claims and abstract) must be numbered consecutively starting with 1. It is desirable to indent paragraphs and to number them (e.g., [0001]). MPEP references provided for more info.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title of invention guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The title of the invention should appear as the heading on the first page of the specification. Although a title may have up to 500 characters, the title must be as short and specific as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively, an introductory portion stating the name, citizenship, residence of each applicant and the title of the invention may appear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference to related applications and priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Any nonprovisional utility application claiming benefit of earlier-filed copending nonprovisional applications or to a provisional under specified statutes must present the reference to the earlier application in an ADS under 37 CFR § 1.76.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR § 1.78 for domestic benefit claims and 37 CFR § 1.55 for foreign priority claims. Cross-references may also be made in an initial section of the description when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement regarding federally sponsored research (when applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention was made with United States government support, the specification must contain a statement specifying that the invention was made with government support and that the U.S. government has certain rights in the invention (per 35 U.S.C. 202(c)(6) and 37 CFR 401.14(f)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example language is provided in the guide to be used in the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to separate materials on read-only optical disc
rubrics_metrics.description: Any material submitted separately on a read-only optical disc (computer program listing appendix, sequence listing, large tables) must be referenced in the specification in a separate incorporation by reference statement and must comply with specified CFR sections (e.g., 37 CFR § 1.52(e), §§ 1.821-1.825, 1.831-1.835, 1.58).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only specified material accepted on read-only optical disc. Total number of discs and files must be specified. Sequence listings and large tables exceeding electronic filing limits have special rules; computer program appendices over 300 lines must be submitted on disc per 37 CFR § 1.96.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background of the invention content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Background section should include a statement of the field of endeavor and a description of information known to you, including references to specific documents related to your invention and problems in the prior art that your invention addresses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.01(c) for more information. Background should preferably identify problems that are then addressed in the summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief summary of the invention content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Brief Summary should present the substance or general idea of the claimed invention in summarized form, include advantages of the invention, and explain how it solves previously existing problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably problems are identified in the Background section. A statement of the object of the invention may be included. See MPEP § 608.01(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of the several views of the drawing
rubrics_metrics.description: Where drawings exist, include a listing of all figures by number (e.g., Figure 1A) with corresponding statements explaining what each figure depicts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If color drawings are present, special language and petition requirements apply; see color drawings criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description requirements and enablement standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Detailed Description must explain the invention and the process of making and using the invention in full, clear, concise, and exact terms, distinguish the invention from prior art, and describe completely the claimed subject matter or improvement. It must enable a person of ordinary skill in the art to make and use the invention without extensive experimentation. Each element in the drawings should be mentioned in the description. The best mode must be disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For improvements, confine description to the specific improvement and cooperating parts necessary. See MPEP § 608.01(g). New matter cannot be added after filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims: form, content, numbering, dependent claims rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must 'particularly point out and distinctly claim' the subject matter regarded as the invention. A nonprovisional application must contain at least one claim. Claims must begin on a separate physical sheet or page and, if multiple, be numbered consecutively in Arabic numerals. Dependent claims may refer back to and limit another claim; dependent claims should be grouped with the claims they refer to. Multiple dependent claims must refer to other claims 'in the alternative' only. Each claim should be a single sentence; elements or steps should be separated by line indentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims define scope of patent protection. The number and type of claims affect fee calculation (excess claims fees). Proper claim drafting and grouping is important for examination and fee purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract of the disclosure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract is intended to enable quick determination of the nature of technical disclosure; it should point out what is new in the art, be in narrative form, generally a single paragraph, must begin on a separate page, and should not be longer than 150 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 608.01(b) for more information. Abstract should succinctly identify the invention's technical contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings necessity and prohibition of adding new matter after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings are required if necessary to understand the subject matter to be patented; drawings must show every feature of the invention as specified in the claims. A drawing necessary to understand the invention cannot be introduced into an application after the filing date because of the prohibition against new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most patent applications contain drawings. Ensure that all claim features that require illustration are included in drawings at filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: General drawing material and medium (black & white normally required)
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are normally required. India ink or equivalent producing black solid lines must be used. Drawings made by hand should be scanned into PDF for filing via Patent Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On rare occasions color drawings may be necessary (see color drawings entry); photographs are not ordinarily permitted but black & white photographs may be accepted where ink drawings are not practical or photographs show invention more clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawing sheet margins and sight size requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For 8.5x11 inch drawing sheets: top margin at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), left at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), right at least 1.5 cm (5/8 inch), bottom at least 1 cm (3/8 inch), leaving a sight no greater than 17.6 cm by 24.4 cm. Similar margins apply for A4 size with slightly different sight dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These margins ensure uniform reproduction and placement of identifying indicia in margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets of drawings and views
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets of drawings should be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1 within the sight; numbers must be placed in the middle of the top of the sheet (or right-hand side if necessary) and be clear and larger than reference characters. Views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1 independent of sheet numbering. Partial views forming one complete view should use the same number with a capital letter (e.g., Figure 1A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where only a single view is used it must not be numbered and 'FIG.' must not appear. Sheet numbering should be shown as 'sheet number/total sheets' (two Arabic numerals separated by an oblique line).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference characters usage rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters not mentioned in the description shall not appear in the drawings; characters mentioned in the description must appear in the drawings. Reference characters (numerals preferred) must be plain, legible, not enclosed, oriented in same direction as view, and at least 0.32 cm (1/8 inch) in height.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference characters should not cross or mingle with lines or be placed on hatched/shaded surfaces; when necessary, underline characters in hatching or leave blank space in hatching. Same part must have same reference character across views; do not reuse characters for different parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead lines and arrows in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead lines (between reference characters and features) may be straight or curved, must originate near the reference character and extend to the feature indicated, should be as short as possible and must not cross each other. Arrows may be used with specific meanings (freestanding arrow indicates entire section toward which it points; arrow touching a line indicates surface looking along arrow direction; arrows can show direction of movement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead lines must be executed like drawing lines and are required except when reference character is on the surface/cross-section (then underline character).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawings (identifying indicia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia on each drawing sheet should include title of the invention, inventor's name, application number (if known), and docket number (if any), placed within the top margin of each sheet. Contact name/telephone may be provided for paper filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information aids USPTO in matching drawings to applications; include when filing drawings in paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms (chemical/math/tables/waveforms) as drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulas, tables, computer program listings, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same drawing requirements. Each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure when necessary. Waveforms must be presented as a single figure using a common vertical axis and time on the horizontal axis; each waveform identified with separate letter designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Groups of waveforms may be in landscape orientation if needed. Characters used must meet character size requirements in 37 CFR § 1.58(c). If computer program listings are lengthy, follow the read-only optical disc requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views, exploded views, partial views, sectional views and related rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must contain as many views as necessary (plan, elevation, section, perspective) and detailed views; exploded views are permissible (embraced by bracket); partial large views may be broken into parts but must be linkable edge-to-edge; sectional views must indicate plane by a broken line with designations and arrows; hatching must indicate materials with regularly spaced oblique parallel lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hatching should not impede readability; breaks in hatching allowed where reference characters inserted. When parts of a view are enlarged, label as separate views; when views on multiple sheets form one view, they must assemble without concealing parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of views and orientation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: One view must not be placed upon or within the outline of another. All views on the same sheet should stand in the same direction and preferably be readable with the sheet upright; words must appear left-to-right when sheet is upright or rotated so top is right side (except standard scientific graphs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If views wider than sheet width are needed, sheet may be turned on its side using appropriate top margin. Avoid connecting views by projection lines and avoid center lines in views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page view requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the views should be suitable for inclusion on the front page of the patent application publication and patent as the illustration of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a clear representative view for front page reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale and prohibition of scale statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be made to a scale large enough to show the mechanism without crowding when reduced to two-thirds reproduction. Indications like 'actual size' or 'scale 1/2' are not permitted because they lose meaning in reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure legibility after reduction; avoid scale notations that do not survive reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of lines, numbers, and letters in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawings must be made by a process giving satisfactory reproduction characteristics: lines, numbers and letters must be durable, clean, black (except color drawings), sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined; weight must permit adequate reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to all lines including fine lines, shading and cut-surface lines. Different line weights may be used where they have different meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading rules in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Shading is encouraged if it aids understanding and does not reduce legibility; used to indicate surface or shape of elements; spaced thin lines preferred for shading; solid black shading is not permitted except for bar graphs or color. Light should come from upper left at about 45 degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shading not preferred for cross-sections. As substitute for shading, heavy lines on shade side may be used except where they obscure reference characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols, legends, and explanatory legends in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical drawing symbols may be used for conventional elements when appropriate and must be adequately identified in the specification. Legends (brief descriptive text) may be used or required by examiner where necessary, containing as few words as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Symbols not universally recognized may be used subject to USPTO approval if not likely to be confused and readily identifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or mask work notice placement and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may appear in the drawing but must be within the sight immediately below the figure representing the copyrighted/mask work material and limited to letters 0.32–0.64 cm (1/8–1/4 inch) high. Content of the notice must be limited to elements provided by law (e.g., '©1983 John Doe').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inclusion of notice permitted only if authorization language at beginning of specification per 37 CFR §1.71(e) is included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized security markings may be placed on drawings provided they are outside the sight, preferably centered in the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep security markings out of the usable drawing area to avoid interfering with reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings and petition requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings are accepted only after the USPTO grants a petition explaining why color is necessary. Petition must include the appropriate fee (37 CFR §1.17(h)), three sets of color drawings, and specific language included as first paragraph in the Brief Description of the Several Views of the Drawing portion of the specification (or an amendment inserting that language).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The required language not in the specification must be added by amendment accompanying the petition. If petition not granted, color drawings may not be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs: limited acceptance and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs are not ordinarily permitted, but black & white photographs will be accepted where ink drawings are not practicable or photographs show the invention more clearly (e.g., gels, blots, cell cultures, histology, animals, plants, imaging). Only one set of black & white photographs is required; no petition or additional fee required for B&W photos. Photographs have same format requirements as drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color photographs require satisfaction of the color drawing petition conditions; photographs must be of sufficient quality for reproduction in patent or publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath or declaration formal requirements and acceptable forms
rubrics_metrics.description: An oath or declaration is required in a nonprovisional application. Either form PTO/AIA/01 or PTO/AIA/08 may be used; PTO/AIA/01 is preferred and must be filed with an ADS. Each inventor must sign an oath/declaration including statutory statements (original inventor status, application made/authorized by inventor) per 35 U.S.C. 115 and 37 CFR § 1.63. An oath must be notarized; a declaration may be submitted in lieu and need not be notarized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature may be handwritten or 'S-signature' (typed name or electronic image between slashes). The oath/declaration must be in a language the inventor understands; substitute statement (Form PTO/AIA/02) may be used for deceased/incapacitated/unavailable/refusing inventors under specified conditions. For continuing applications, copy of earlier oath/declaration may be used if it complies with current rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitute statement rules for missing inventor signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: A substitute statement may be signed by the applicant when an inventor is deceased, legally incapacitated, cannot be found after diligent effort, or has refused to execute the oath/declaration. Joint inventors who are the applicant may sign substitute statements for inventors who cannot be found or have refused, but not for deceased or legally incapacitated inventors. A legal representative or assignee who is the applicant may sign for deceased or legally incapacitated inventors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTO/AIA/02 is the USPTO substitute statement form for these situations; follow the statutory/regulatory requirements (see guide text for details).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: For disclosures of nucleotide or amino acid sequences, a sequence listing must comply with 37 CFR §§1.821–1.825 and may be in paper or electronic form; if exceeding filing system limits, it may be submitted on read-only optical disc per applicable CFR sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after July 1, 2022, sequence listing XML requirements apply. If submitted on disc, specification must contain an incorporation by reference to the disc and list number of discs and files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining a receipt for mailed or hand-delivered documents (postcard receipt)
rubrics_metrics.description: A receipt for mailed/hand-delivered documents can be obtained by attaching a stamped, self-addressed postcard to the first page of the documents containing a detailed list identifying each document type and number of pages. The USPTO will compare the list to contents, annotate discrepancies, initial and date stamp the postcard, and return it as evidence of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postcard must include identifying info (application number, confirmation number, filing date if known, title, inventor name(s)) and detailed list of each component and page counts. General statements like 'complete application' will not suffice. Returned postcard annotated that an item was not received will not serve as evidence for that item.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express filing date rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 35 U.S.C. 21 and 37 CFR § 1.10, correspondence delivered via USPS 'Priority Mail Express Post Office to Addressee' will be considered filed on the date of deposit with USPS as shown on the mailing label or official USPS notation; if deposit date cannot be determined, the Office receipt date is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the number of the mailing label on the application papers and mail only one application per Priority Mail Express package. This provides a means to establish filing date when mailing to USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-on correspondence and registered eFiler requirements to avoid fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent correspondence filed after the application filing date by mail or hand-delivery can avoid the $400 non-electronic filing fee. However, if you receive a 'Notice of Incomplete Application' assigning an application number but no filing date, you must become a registered eFiler and file the reply via Patent Center to avoid the $400 non-electronic filing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learn how to become a registered eFiler via USPTO Getting Started guide or call Electronic Business Center. Follow-on correspondence filed by anyone other than a registered eFiler must be mailed or hand-delivered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content detail requirements when mailing with postcard
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a postcard with a mailed patent application, the detailed listing should include title and number of pages of each USPTO form; number of pages of specification (excluding claims); number of claims and claim pages; number of drawing figures and sheets; whether an oath/declaration is included and its page count; types and numbers of other documents and page counts; payment amount and method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postcard must itemize each component precisely; failure to itemize may cause postcard not to serve as evidence for missing items. The USPTO will stamp the postcard with receipt date and application number before returning it.
